proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6261 *dādda compares Bengali, Assamese, Hindi and Marathi dādā “elder brother”, Kalasha dāda “father” and other older-relative senses. This is a nursery kinship family; the link does not assert that every regional use was inherited without contact.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 1008 ākāśa gives Pali/Prakrit ākāsa “sky” and discusses Dardic outcomes separately. Retained-k sky forms identify this lexical family, though learned restoration or intra-IA transmission may account for conservatism; the provisional link does not assert uninterrupted inheritance.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 6225 davara/dōra/ḍōra gives Prakrit dōra/ḍōra, Punjabi ḍorā, Nepali ḍoro “thread” and ḍori “rope”, Bhojpuri ḍorā and Gujarati/Marathi dor/dorī. Both dental and retroflex initials are explicitly represented; their local transmission remains open.
